1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build or improve the existing game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Check that the game runs correctly, clean up bugs, and make reactions reflect real research while adding procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, playable game or apply the changes to the existing game.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify using screenshots saved as small JPEGs, at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State

- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the existing game and determine its current implementation and run/test workflow.
2. Implement the archival and cross-cell incorporation gameplay, with research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
3. Run the game and relevant checks, fix issues, and capture a latest-check JPEG screenshot.

- No files have been inspected or changed yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Check that the game runs correctly, clean up bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game; deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as small JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the project’s main HTML, JavaScript, and CSS files; identified an existing GENESIS living-genome game and archive view.

### Active
- Determine the game’s implementation and run/test workflow, then implement archival and cross-cell incorporation gameplay with research-informed reactions and procedural effects.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining game code and available run/test workflow.
2. Implement and integrate archival and cross-cell part incorporation.
3. Run the game and relevant checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest-check JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and navigation.
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive view, and interactions.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` includes an archive view with genome saving, exporting, and seeding worlds; parts archiving and cross-cell incorporation are not yet confirmed.
- No files have been changed, and no tests or screenshot verification have been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable, fix bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the main game files and found an existing genome archive with genome saving, exporting, and seeding worlds.

### Active
- Determine the run/test workflow, then implement archival and cross-cell incorporation of parts and DNA.
- Run checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game logic and the available run/test workflow.
2. Implement archive and cross-cell part incorporation with research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
3. Run relevant checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive view, and interactions.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` includes an archive view; part archiving and cross-cell incorporation are not yet confirmed.
- No files have been changed, and no tests or screenshot verification have been performed.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable, fix bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected key game files and confirmed the app has a genome archive with genome saving, exporting, and seeding worlds.

### Active
- Determine the run/test workflow, then implement archival and cross-cell incorporation of parts and DNA.
- Run checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game logic and the available run/test workflow.
2. Implement archive and cross-cell part incorporation with research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
3. Run relevant checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive view, and interactions.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` includes an archive view; part archiving and cross-cell incorporation are not yet confirmed.
- No files have been changed, and no tests or screenshot verification have been performed.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable, fix bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the project files and confirmed the app has a genome archive with genome saving, exporting, and seeding worlds.
- Identified `start.sh` and `capture.sh` as project start and screenshot scripts.

### Active
- Determine the run/test workflow, then implement archival and cross-cell incorporation of parts and DNA.
- Run checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game logic and the available run/test workflow.
2. Implement archive and cross-cell part incorporation with research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
3. Run relevant checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive view, cell plate, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` includes an archive view; part archiving and cross-cell incorporation are not yet confirmed.
- No files have been changed, and no tests or screenshot verification have been performed.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable, fix bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the project has an existing genome archive with genome saving, exporting, and world seeding.
- Identified `start.sh` and `capture.sh` as project run and screenshot scripts.
- Confirmed the working tree has no reported changes.

### Active
- Inspect remaining game logic and determine the run/test workflow.
- Implement archival and cross-cell incorporation of parts and DNA, plus research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect archive, cell, and reaction logic to identify existing functionality and gaps.
2. Implement part and DNA archiving and cross-cell incorporation, along with reaction improvements.
3. Run relevant checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive view, cell plate, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` includes an archive view with genome saving and “SEED WORLD” controls; part archiving and cross-cell incorporation are not yet confirmed.
- No files have been changed, and no tests or screenshot verification have been performed.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable, fix bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Located the existing genome archive and confirmed it supports genome saving, exporting, and world seeding.
- Identified `start.sh` and `capture.sh` as project run and screenshot scripts.
- Confirmed the working tree has no reported changes.

### Active
- Inspect archive, cell, and reaction logic to identify existing functionality and gaps.
- Implement part and DNA archiving and cross-cell incorporation, along with research-informed reactions and procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining game logic and determine the run/test workflow.
2. Implement archival and cross-cell incorporation of parts and DNA, along with reaction improvements.
3. Run relevant checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive view, cell plate, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` includes an archive view with genome saving and “SEED WORLD” controls; part archiving and cross-cell incorporation are not yet confirmed.
- No files have been changed, and no tests or screenshot verification have been performed.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable, fix bugs, and make reactions research-informed with procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/export, and archived-genome plate-loading functionality.
- Reviewed relevant archive, plate, and lab logic; confirmed archived genomes can seed worlds or be loaded as cells on the plate.

### Active
- Implement DNA and cellular-part archiving and cross-cell incorporation.
- Review reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive, cell plate, lab, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.

- Element markers are explicitly visual-only and do not alter cell metrics; do not present them as biological reactions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/export, and archived-genome plate-loading functionality.
- Reviewed relevant archive, plate, and lab logic; confirmed archived genomes can seed worlds or be loaded as cells on the plate.

### Active
- Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
- Review reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
2. Review reaction behavior and improve it with research-informed effects; do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive, cell plate, lab, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.
- Element markers are explicitly visual-only and do not alter cell metrics; do not present them as biological reactions.
- `node --check app.js` passed before changes; no changes have been made yet.

- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- No additional decisions yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/export, and archived-genome plate-loading functionality.
- Reviewed relevant archive, plate, and lab logic; confirmed archived genomes can seed worlds or be loaded as cells on the plate.

### Active
- Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
- Review reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
2. Review reaction behavior and improve it with research-informed effects.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive, cell plate, lab, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.
- `node --check app.js` passed before changes; no changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Located the genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/export, and archived-genome plate-loading functionality.
- Reviewed relevant archive, plate, and lab logic; confirmed archived genomes can seed worlds or be loaded as cells on the plate.

### Active
- Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
- Review reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
2. Review reaction behavior and improve it with research-informed effects.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive, cell plate, lab, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.
- `node --check app.js` passed before changes; no changes have been made yet.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Located and reviewed the genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/loading, and related game interactions.

### Active
- Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
- Review reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
2. Review reaction behavior and improve it with research-informed effects.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive, cell plate, lab, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Located and reviewed the genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/loading, and related game interactions.

### Active
- Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
- Review reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement DNA and cellular-part archive/incorporation functionality.
2. Review reaction behavior and improve it with research-informed effects.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, archive, cell plate, lab, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Located and reviewed the genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/loading, and related interactions.

### Active
- Implement cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer alongside the existing genome archive.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural improvements without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Improve cell reactions with research-informed procedural effects while keeping visual-only markers clearly distinct.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, genome archive, cell plate, lab, interactions, and persistent state.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.
- `handleAction` includes `add-element-plate`, which adds visual-only `elementExposures` markers and reports them as sandbox markers; these do not alter cell metrics.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive DNA sequences and cellular parts, then incorporate them into other cells.
- Make the game playable and improve reactions with research-informed procedural effects.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- (none)

## Work State
### Completed
- Located and reviewed the genome archive, cell plate, genome saving/loading, and related interactions.

### Active
- Implement cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer alongside the existing genome archive.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Improve cell reactions with research-informed procedural effects while keeping visual-only markers clearly distinct.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, genome archive, cell plate, lab, interactions, and persistent state.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving currently requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- Plate actions include adding live cells, loading archived cells, inspecting a cell genome, and removing cells; cellular-part archiving and cross-cell transfer are not implemented.
- `handleAction` includes `add-element-plate`, which adds visual-only `elementExposures` markers and reports them as sandbox markers; these do not alter cell metrics.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed existing genome archive, cell plate, cell genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `handleAction` includes `add-element-plate`, which adds persistent `elementExposures` markers and triggers a brief halo; markers do not affect cell metrics.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed existing genome archive, cell plate, cell genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `handleAction` includes `add-element-plate`, which adds persistent `elementExposures` markers and triggers a brief halo; markers do not affect cell metrics.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed the existing genome archive, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, cell reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `handleAction` includes `add-element-plate`, which adds persistent `elementExposures` markers and triggers a brief halo; markers do not affect cell metrics.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- Cell defaults are initialized in `makePlateState()` and state normalization; `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics.
- No implementation changes or verification have been made yet.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs at most 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed the existing genome archive, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, cell reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `handleAction` includes `add-element-plate`, which adds persistent `elementExposures` markers and triggers a brief halo; markers do not affect cell metrics.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- Cell defaults are initialized in `makePlateState()` and state normalization; `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics.
- `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` reports model states such as low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates ROS, protein load, ATP, and damage.
- No implementation changes or verification have been made yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only and the UI explicitly says they do not represent dose, reactions, or biological effects.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, cell reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- Cell defaults are initialized in `makePlateState()` and state normalization; `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics.
- `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` reports model states such as low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates ROS, protein load, ATP, and damage.
- No implementation changes or verification have been made yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only and the UI explicitly says they do not represent dose, reactions, or biological effects.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes; no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, cell reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- Cell defaults are initialized in `makePlateState()` and state normalization; `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics.
- `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` reports model states such as low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates ROS, protein load, ATP, and damage.

## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Confirmed element markers are visual-only and the UI explicitly says they do not represent dose, reactions, or biological effects.
- Confirmed `node --check app.js` passes; no implementation changes have been made.

### Active
- Add cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement cellular-part archiving and transfer between cells.
2. Add research-informed cell effects without misrepresenting visual markers as biological reactions.
3. Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, genome archive, cell plate, cell reactions, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- The cell plate supports adding live or archived-genome cells, inspecting a cell genome, staining, cell-cycle advancement, and removal.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- Cell defaults are initialized in `makePlateState()` and state normalization; `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics.
- `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` reports model states such as low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates ROS, protein load, ATP, and damage.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, archiving, and installation helpers in `app.js`.

### Active
- Add interface and action handling for archiving parts and transferring them between cells.
- Ensure installed-part state persists, survives normalization, and affects only clearly labeled model proxies.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, fix issues, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `makePlateState()` now initializes `metabolicActivity` and `installedParts`.
- New helpers: `partDefinition`, `installedPart`, `partQuality`, `cellPartQuality`, `archiveCellPart`, and `installCellPart`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity. UI/actions and persistence initialization remain unconnected.

input.pattern: CELL_PART_TYPES|partArchive|function archiveView|function cellView|function bind|addEventListener|function save|localStorage|function normalize|archiveCellPart|installCellPart

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and incorporate them into other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, archiving, and installation helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add interface and action handling for archiving parts and transferring them between cells.
- Ensure installed-part state persists, survives normalization, and affects only clearly labeled model proxies.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, fix issues, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `makePlateState()` initializes `metabolicActivity` and `installedParts`.
- New helpers: `partDefinition`, `installedPart`, `partQuality`, `cellPartQuality`, `archiveCellPart`, and `installCellPart`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity. UI/actions and persistence initialization remain unconnected.
- `app.js` has uncommitted changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, archiving, and installation helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add interface and action handling for archiving parts and transferring them between cells.
- Ensure installed-part state persists, survives normalization, and affects only clearly labeled model proxies.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture a JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, fix issues, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- Helpers `partDefinition`, `installedPart`, `partQuality`, `cellPartQuality`, `archiveCellPart`, and `installCellPart` exist; `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`, and `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity.
- UI/actions and persistence initialization remain unconnected; `app.js` has uncommitted changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells, alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State

### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, and archiving/installing helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
- Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
- Run checks, fix issues, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, including target-cell selection and feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and persistence.
3. Add research-informed cell effects without implying visual-only element markers are biological reactions.
4. Run checks, capture a compliant JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- Helpers `partDefinition`, `installedPart`, `partQuality`, `cellPartQuality`, `archiveCellPart`, and `installCellPart` exist; `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`, and `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity.
- `app.js` contains uncommitted changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, and archive/install helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
- Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects without conflating them with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, including target-cell selection and feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and persistence.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, capture a compliant JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- Helpers `partDefinition`, `installedPart`, `partQuality`, `cellPartQuality`, `archiveCellPart`, and `installCellPart` exist; `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`, and `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity.
- `app.js` has uncommitted changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, and archive/install helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
- Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects without conflating them with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, including target-cell selection and feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and persistence.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, capture a compliant JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity.
- The cellular-part helpers are not yet connected to UI actions; `cellView()` has an organelle registry suitable for exposing installed-part status and controls.
- `app.js` has uncommitted changes.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, and archive/install helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
- Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects without conflating them with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, including target-cell selection and feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and persistence.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, capture a compliant JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity.
- The cellular-part helpers are not yet connected to UI actions; `cellView()` has an organelle registry suitable for exposing installed-part status and controls.
