messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, and archive/install helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
- Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects without conflating them with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, including target-cell selection and feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and persistence.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, capture a compliant JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity.
- The cellular-part helpers are not yet connected to UI actions; `cellView()` has an organelle registry suitable for exposing installed-part status and controls.

## Objective
- Complete the existing GENESIS game so players can archive cellular parts and install them in other cells alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while clearly distinguishing visual-only markers from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game and deliver a complete, playable result.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records represent educational model proxies; installing one currently blends its quality into a corresponding cell metric.
- Cellular-part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reviewed genome archiving, cell plate, genome loading, cell interactions, and element marker behavior.
- Added cellular-part metadata, cell quality capture, and archive/install helpers in `app.js`.
- Confirmed `app.js` passes `node --check`.

### Active
- Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, with target-cell selection and success/error feedback.
- Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and ensure state initialization and persistence preserve installed parts.
- Review cell reactions and add research-informed procedural effects without conflating them with visual-only element markers.
- Run checks, capture and inspect the required JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add archive and transfer controls to the cell observatory and archive view, including target-cell selection and feedback.
2. Connect part archive/install helpers to UI actions and persistence.
3. Add research-informed cell effects while preserving the visual-only distinction for element markers.
4. Run checks, capture a compliant JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game state, archive/install helpers, views, and simulation behavior.
- `index.html`: Game structure and navigation.
- `style.css`: Game styling.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture script.
- `start.sh`: Project start script.

## Important Context
- Genome archiving requires a sequenced genome; archive records can seed worlds, export/import, or be loaded onto the cell plate.
- `S.plateSources` maps genome IDs to genome records; cells reference their genome with `genomeId`.
- `archiveView()` currently archives genomes only; `plate-archive` adds cells from an archived genome.
- `cellView()` displays organelle and cell metrics; `cycleCheckpoint(cell)` checks low ATP, DNA damage, membrane damage, and apoptosis; `advancePlateCells()` updates cell proxies.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` appends a proxy record to `S.partArchive`; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects duplicate part types and blends proxy quality into ATP, membrane integrity, protein load, or metabolic activity. Helpers are not yet connected to UI actions.
- Current repository state has an uncommitted modification to `app.js`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while keeping visual-only element markers distinct from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, playable result in the existing game.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, and state initialization for part archives and installed parts.
- Added cell-observatory controls to archive a part proxy and select an archived proxy and target cell for installation.
- Added cellular-part archive records and target selection to the genome archive view.
- Connected archive and install actions, including duplicate-part and source-cell transfer checks.
- Added proxy indicators to relevant organelle registry readings and included part records in database export.
- Kept element marker descriptions explicit that they are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.

### Active
- Finish styling and review the new cellular-part controls.
- Verify part archiving, transfer, persistence, duplicate handling, and simulation behavior.
- Run checks and capture/inspect the required compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add responsive styling for `.part-workbench`, `.part-transfer-controls`, and `.part-note` in `style.css`.
2. Run `node --check app.js` and exercise cellular-part archive/install paths, including persistence and duplicate/source-cell errors.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px using the project capture workflow and inspect the latest screenshot.
4. Summarize the result and briefly note the educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: State, simulation, observatory/archive views, and cellular-part actions.
- `style.css`: Existing visual system; needs styling for the new controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`; screenshot verification and styling are still pending.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` archives a proxy from the selected cell; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transferring to its source cell and duplicate part types.
- Export now includes `partArchive` and `partSequence`; import behavior for cellular-part records has not been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while keeping visual-only element markers distinct from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, playable result in the existing game.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, and state initialization for part archives and installed parts.
- Added cell-observatory controls to archive a part proxy and select an archived proxy and target cell for installation.
- Added cellular-part archive records and target selection to the genome archive view.
- Connected archive and install actions, including duplicate-part and source-cell transfer checks.
- Added proxy indicators to relevant organelle registry readings and included part records in database export.
- Kept element marker descriptions explicit that they are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- `node --check app.js` passes.

### Active
- Style and review `.part-workbench`, `.part-transfer-controls`, and `.part-note` in `style.css`.
- Verify cellular-part archive/install paths, persistence, duplicate/source-cell errors, and simulation behavior; inspect import behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add responsive styling for the cellular-part controls.
2. Exercise archive/install, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, and simulation behavior; confirm import/export handling.
3. Run checks and capture/inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize the result and briefly note the educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Cellular-part state, simulation, observatory/archive views, and archive/install actions.
- `style.css`: Existing visual system; needs styling for the new controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`; styling and screenshot verification remain pending.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` archives a proxy from the selected cell; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transferring to its source cell and duplicate part types.
- Export includes `partArchive` and `partSequence`; import behavior for cellular-part records has not been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving.
- Add research-informed procedural cell effects while keeping visual-only element markers distinct from biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, playable result in the existing game.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, and state initialization for part archives and installed parts.
- Added cell-observatory controls to archive a part proxy and select an archived proxy and target cell for installation.
- Added cellular-part archive records and target selection to the genome archive view.
- Connected archive and install actions, including duplicate-part and source-cell transfer checks.
- Added proxy indicators to relevant organelle registry readings and included part records in database export.
- Kept element marker descriptions explicit that they are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- `node --check app.js` passes.

### Active
- Add responsive styling for `.part-workbench`, `.part-transfer-controls`, and `.part-note` in `style.css`.
- Verify archive/install paths, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, simulation behavior, and import/export handling.
- Run checks and capture/inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add responsive styling for cellular-part controls.
2. Test archive/install, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, simulation behavior, and import behavior.
3. Run checks and capture/inspect the latest JPEG screenshot within the stated width limit.
4. Summarize the result and briefly note educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Cellular-part state, simulation, observatory/archive views, and archive/install actions.
- `style.css`: Existing visual system; needs styling for the new controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js`; styling and screenshot verification remain pending.
- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines `mitochondria`, `membrane`, `endoplasmic-reticulum`, and `cytoplasm`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` archives a proxy from the selected cell; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transferring to its source cell and duplicate part types.
- Export includes `partArchive` and `partSequence`; import currently reads genome records only and needs verification/consideration for part records.

## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving, with research-informed procedural cell effects and clear separation between visual-only element markers and biological reactions.

## Requirements
- Deliver a complete, playable result in the existing game.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Do not present visual-only element markers as biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, state initialization, observatory controls, archive records, target selection, and proxy indicators.
- Added responsive styling for `.part-workbench`, `.part-transfer-controls`, and `.part-note` in `style.css`.
- Extended JSON import to accept genome archives, standalone genomes, and cellular-part records; validates records and deduplicates imported genomes, parts, and notebook entries.
- Export includes `partArchive`, `partSequence`, and notebook records.
- Preserved explicit visual-only element-marker descriptions.
- `node --check app.js` passes.

### Active
- Verify archive/install workflows, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, simulation behavior, and import/export handling.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the application and test archive/install, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, simulation inheritance, and database import/export.
2. Run checks and capture/inspect the latest JPEG screenshot within the 1280px width limit.
3. Summarize the result and briefly note the educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Cellular-part state, simulation, observatory/archive views, and archive/install/import/export actions.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling for cellular-part controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted in `app.js` and `style.css`.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` archives a proxy from the selected cell; `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transfers to the source cell and duplicate part types.
- Import validation errors include `No genome or cellular-part archive records found`, `An imported genome is missing its sequence or gene annotations`, and `An imported cellular-part record is incomplete or unsupported`.

## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving, with research-informed procedural cell effects.
- Deliver a playable result and verify key workflows and appearance.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Clearly distinguish visual-only element markers from biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, state initialization, observatory controls, archive records, target selection, and proxy indicators.
- Added responsive styling, import validation and deduplication for genomes, cellular parts, and notebook entries; export includes `partArchive`, `partSequence`, and notebook records.
- Preserved explicit visual-only element-marker descriptions.
- Confirmed daughter-cell creation copies installed proxies in `dividePlateCell`; `node --check app.js` passes.

### Active
- Verify archive/install workflows, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, simulation inheritance, and database import/export.
- Run the app, capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot, and run relevant checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the application and test archive/install, persistence, rejection cases, inheritance, and import/export.
2. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot within the 1280px width limit.
3. Summarize results and briefly note the educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Cellular-part state, simulation, archive/install/import/export, and UI actions.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling for cellular-part controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js` and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transfer to the source cell and duplicate part types.
- Import validation errors include `No genome or cellular-part archive records found`, `An imported genome is missing its sequence or gene annotations`, and `An imported cellular-part record is incomplete or unsupported`.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving, with research-informed procedural cell effects.
- Deliver a playable result and verify key workflows and appearance.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Clearly distinguish visual-only element markers from biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, state initialization, observatory controls, archive records, target selection, and proxy indicators.
- Added responsive styling, import validation and deduplication for genomes, cellular parts, and notebook entries; export includes `partArchive`, `partSequence`, and notebook records.
- Preserved explicit visual-only element-marker descriptions.
- Confirmed daughter-cell creation copies installed proxies in `dividePlateCell`; `node --check app.js` passes.
- Reviewed the start/capture scripts and relevant app state, archive, and transfer logic.

### Active
- Verify archive/install workflows, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, inheritance, and database import/export.
- Run the app, capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot, and run relevant checks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the application and test archive/install, persistence, rejection cases, inheritance, and import/export.
2. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot within the 1280px width limit.
3. Summarize results and briefly note the educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Cellular-part state, simulation, archive/install/import/export, and UI actions.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling for cellular-part controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.
- `index.html`: App shell and navigation.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js` and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transfer to the source cell and duplicate part types.
- Import validation errors include `No genome or cellular-part archive records found`, `An imported genome is missing its sequence or gene annotations`, and `An imported cellular-part record is incomplete or unsupported`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete GENESIS’s cellular-part archive and transfer alongside genome archiving, with research-informed procedural cell effects.
- Deliver a playable result and verify key workflows and appearance.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Verify with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot unless fine detail requires a full-size PNG.
- Clearly distinguish visual-only element markers from biological reactions.

## Decisions
- Element plate markers are visual-only and do not alter cell metrics.
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies; installing one blends its quality into simplified cell metrics.
- Part types are mitochondria, cell membrane, endoplasmic reticulum, and cytoplasm; OpenStax Biology 2e is cited as the source.
- Installed proxies carry forward to daughter cells and make small, model-only adjustments to simulation dynamics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added cellular-part metadata, quality capture, archive/install helpers, state initialization, observatory controls, archive records, target selection, and proxy indicators.
- Added responsive styling, import validation and deduplication for genomes, cellular parts, and notebook entries; export includes `partArchive`, `partSequence`, and notebook records.
- Preserved explicit visual-only element-marker descriptions.
- Confirmed daughter-cell creation copies installed proxies in `dividePlateCell`; `node --check app.js` passes.
- Started the app at `http://localhost:3000`, opened it in Playwright, and navigated to the cell observatory using `[data-view=cell]`.

### Active
- Verify archive/install workflows, persistence, duplicate/source-cell rejection, inheritance, and database import/export.
- Capture and inspect the latest compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Browser verification is incomplete; Playwright initially reported missing Chromium, but Chromium was installed and the browser opened successfully.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing of archive/install, persistence, rejection cases, inheritance, and import/export.
2. Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot within the 1280px width limit.
3. Summarize results and briefly note the educational-proxy assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Cellular-part state, simulation, archive/install/import/export, and UI actions.
- `style.css`: Responsive styling for cellular-part controls.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Project start entry point.
- `index.html`: App shell and navigation.

## Important Context
- Changes in `app.js` and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- `installCellPart(record, cell)` rejects transfer to the source cell and duplicate part types.
- Import validation errors include `No genome or cellular-part archive records found`, `An imported genome is missing its sequence or gene annotations`, and `An imported cellular-part record is incomplete or unsupported`.
- Browser startup showed one console error: missing `/favicon.ico` (404).

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS into a procedurally generated game grounded in real-life biology, rather than an educational simulation.

## Requirements
- Make the entire game procedurally generated and based on real-life biology.
- Preserve accurate distinctions between biological processes and visual-only elements.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not actual organelles or biological treatments.
- No broader redesign decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cellular-part archive and transfer features were previously implemented and browser-verified.

### Active
- Inspect and redesign existing game systems and framing to meet the procedural, biologically grounded goal.

### Blocked
- An earlier architecture review failed with `Copilot /auto returned HTTP 502`; no findings were returned.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current game systems and identify changes needed to shift from educational-simulation framing to procedural generation grounded in real-life biology.
2. Implement the redesign and verify it in the browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, simulation, archive, and UI actions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and simulation framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `style.css` have uncommitted changes from earlier cellular-part work.
- The latest recorded browser screenshot is `screenshots/cell-observatory.jpg` (JPEG, 1050×793); a non-blocking `/favicon.ico` 404 was noted.

- Rework GENESIS into a procedurally generated game grounded in real-life biology, rather than an educational simulation.

## Requirements
- Make the entire game procedurally generated and based on real-life biology.
- Preserve accurate distinctions between biological processes and visual-only elements.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not actual organelles or biological treatments.
- No broader redesign decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cellular-part archive and transfer features were previously implemented and browser-verified.

### Active
- Inspect and redesign existing game systems and framing to meet the procedural, biologically grounded goal.

### Blocked

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current game systems and identify changes needed to shift from educational-simulation framing to procedural generation grounded in real-life biology.
2. Implement the redesign and verify it in the browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, simulation, archive, and UI actions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and simulation framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `style.css` have uncommitted changes from earlier cellular-part work.
- The latest recorded browser screenshot is `screenshots/cell-observatory.jpg` (JPEG, 1050×793); a non-blocking `/favicon.ico` 404 was noted.
- Current `app.js` describes GENESIS as a deterministic educational model. It includes a seeded RNG, cellular function/part definitions, and plate-cell simulation logic.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e42cced44ffe9OdwnnJn4BJ6Jm" state="completed">
## Review

**GENESIS currently uses procedural generation to vary a deterministic educational model; it does not yet simulate a procedurally generated biological world.** Its seed controls synthetic genomes, initial conditions, and repeatable random variation, but most outcomes come from hand-authored formulas and thresholds.

A key architectural issue is that the app maintains **two overlapping simulation scales**: a global population/genome model and a separate observatory-plate model. The global simulation advances its own genome and population summary, while individual plate cells have their own division and mutation logic. Those systems are related in presentation but are not one coherent evolving population.

## What is biological, abstracted, or visual

| System | What it does now | How to characterize it |
|---|---|---|
| Genome generation | Creates seeded base sequences, gene-like records, regulatory labels, and activity values. | **Procedural abstraction.** The genes and sequences are invented; translation uses a custom mapping, not a biologically faithful gene-to-protein model. |
| Gene expression and traits | Applies simple rules for nutrient/stress responses and converts expression into values such as energy metabolism and repair. | **Biology-inspired heuristic.** Expression is not driven by a mechanistic regulatory network, and trait values are proxies. |
| Cell health and division | Updates ATP, ROS, damage, membrane integrity, viability, and a staged cell-cycle meter with formulas, thresholds, and seeded noise. | **Cell-biology-themed model.** The names evoke real processes, but the equations, units, and thresholds are not established as predictive biology. |
| Mutation and evolution | Mutates plate-cell genomes at division; separately, the aggregate genome changes during generation steps. | **Computational inheritance and variation**, but not a unified population-genetics model. Plate daughters and aggregate generations follow distinct rules. |
| Environment and population | Adjusts environmental variables and scalar population, fitness, and diversity summaries. | **Game abstractions.** Current population and fitness calculations are not derived from tracked organism interactions or validated ecological dynamics. |
| Archived cellular parts | Saves a cell-derived quality score and uses it to adjust a target cell’s proxy metrics. | **Explicit proxy mechanic**, not organelle transfer or transplantation biology. |
| Ecosystem display | Draws seeded dots whose glow pulses with the tick. | **Visual-only representation.** The dots are not spatially simulated organisms. |
| Element markers | Adds a marker and brief halo to a selected cell. | **Explicitly visual-only.** The UI says these markers do not model dose, reaction, or biological effect. |
| Wet-lab outputs | Produces simulated estimates and some proxy measurements. | **Game output, not experimental data.** The estimates should be clearly identified as generated by the model. |

The footer already says “SIMPLIFIED RESEARCH MODEL · NOT A PREDICTIVE BIOLOGICAL MODEL,” which is a useful safeguard. However, the research-station framing and biological terminology can still make individual mechanics sound more realistic than they are.

## Recommended changes

### 1. Make one simulation the source of truth

Choose whether the main game is about a population of individual cells or a higher-level population summary.

For a cellular evolution game, make individual organisms the authoritative state: derive population size, diversity, fitness, and lineage summaries from their genomes and states. Avoid separately advancing a global genome unless that is explicitly a different, named model.

If both scales are important, define their relationship in the architecture and UI—for example, a population model with a clearly labeled sample of observable cells—rather than letting both appear to represent the same population.

### 2. Choose a biological scope before increasing detail

A useful initial scope would be a **single, specified microbial life-history model** in a bounded habitat. That makes it easier to define what the simulated organism is, how it reproduces, what resources it consumes, and what claims the model can support.

Treat the simulation as **biology-grounded game modeling**, not a general-purpose “real cell” simulator. Avoid adding biological labels unless the underlying mechanic has a defined interpretation.

### 3. Tie procedural generation to coherent rules

Use procedural generation to produce playable variation within explicit constraints, rather than merely generating more random genome fields. For example, vary starting conditions, organism parameters, or habitat layouts while preserving defined ranges and tradeoffs.

For any generated trait, document:

- What biological concept it represents.
- Which state variables affect it.
- How it affects survival or reproduction.
- Whether its values or effects are based on sources, simplified assumptions, or game balancing.

Keep generated sequences clearly fictional unless they correspond to real genes or organisms.

### 4. Connect inheritance, phenotype, and selection

Make a mutation affect a defined trait through an explicit model, then make that trait affect survival or reproductive success under the current conditions. Track inherited variants and their frequencies across the population. This would give selection and evolution a visible causal path instead of relying primarily on a separate aggregate fitness score.

If the model does not support a particular biological mechanism—such as recombination, gene transfer, or detailed gene regulation—label it as absent or abstracted rather than implying it through realistic-sounding genome displays.

### 5. Separate model rules from UI and visual effects

Structure the simulation so model state transitions, seeded randomness, and rendering are distinct. This would make it easier to inspect whether a change affects biology-model behavior or only presentation, and to test the simulation without relying on the interface.

Keep visual elements such as ecosystem particles, cell animation, staining effects, and element markers in a presentation layer. The UI can still make them engaging, but should not imply that they represent spatial ecology or chemical effects unless those mechanics are actually modeled.

### 6. Define model units, assumptions, and checks

For values presented with units or biological names, specify whether they are measured values, normalized game variables, or proxies. Document the equations and thresholds that drive cell-cycle progression, viability, and reproduction.

Add checks for reproducibility and basic model behavior: the same seed should produce the same run; state values should remain in valid bounds; and population or resource changes should follow the stated rules. This would improve trust without overstating scientific validity.

### 7. Make the framing consistent throughout the product

Keep the existing non-predictive disclaimer, and extend the same distinction to the genome, observatory, evolution, and wet-lab views. In particular, distinguish:

- **Biological process modeled** — behavior represented by an explicit simulation rule.
- **Simplified proxy** — a related concept represented with a game variable or heuristic.
- **Visual-only** — presentation that does not alter model state.

The README is still OMGithub boilerplate, so it currently does not explain the game’s scope, model assumptions, or which features are visual-only.

## Files reviewed

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js` — seeded generation, genome and trait heuristics, both simulation scales, cell division, population updates, lab outputs, and visual-only mechanics.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` — research-station framing and the simplified/non-predictive disclaimer.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md` — project documentation, currently boilerplate.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css` — presentation and responsive styling.

No files were modified.
</subagent>

input.prompt: Inspect current app.js, index.html, style.css. Identify architecture and concrete minimal changes to shift the game from invented genome/lab simulator framing toward procedural ecosystem grounded in real biology. Preserve prior cellular-part archive/transfer work and avoid broad rewrite if possible. Return key functions/data shapes and implementation recommendations.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e42c6a419ffeeWrUq1378jaX06" state="completed">
## Architecture

The app is a small, dependency-free single-page application. [`index.html`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html) provides the sidebar, navigation, shared status areas, and `#view-root`; [`app.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/app.js) contains the state, simulation, view rendering, persistence, and user actions; [`style.css`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css) handles the theme and responsive layout. Views are rendered into `#view-root` by `render()`, with navigation and actions handled in the same script. The README contains project links rather than architecture documentation.

The app presents itself as a **simplified educational model, not a predictive biological model**—a useful framing to retain as the simulation grows.

### State and simulation flow

- `initialState(seed, source)` builds the world-level state: a genome, environment, aggregate population and fitness measures, history and events, research records, and a starter observatory plate.
- `makeGenome(seed, source)` creates annotated genes and sequence data. `makePlateState(...)` creates individual cell records and a genome lookup in `plateSources`.
- The environment tracks temperature, radiation, nutrients, oxygen, water, pH, and chemical exposure. `environmentStress()` and `traitMap()` turn some of those values and gene annotations into model inputs.
- `tick()` advances the aggregate world measures; `advancePlateCells()` separately updates observatory cells. A 650 ms interval runs ticks while playing, with the selected speed controlling how many ticks run per interval.
- The plate cells have their own viability, ATP, damage, membrane, stress, cycle, and lineage fields. Cell division uses `cycleCheckpoint()`, `dividePlateCell()`, and `mutatePlateGenome()`.
- Separately, `generationStep()` periodically mutates the world-level genome and updates aggregate history. This means the app currently has **two related but distinct evolutionary tracks**: aggregate-world generations and per-cell plate lineages.
- `storeState()` saves browser-local state under `genesis-living-genome-v1`, omitting the `playing` flag; `loadState()` restores it and startup code supplies defaults for several missing plate fields.

### Cellular-part archive and transfer

The existing archive/transfer flow is localized and can be preserved:

- `CELL_PART_TYPES` defines four transferable **model proxies**: mitochondria/ATP, membrane/integrity, endoplasmic reticulum/folding, and cytoplasm/metabolic activity.
- `archiveCellPart(typeId)` records the selected cell’s proxy quality and provenance, including its source cell and genome.
- `installCellPart(record, cell)` applies that recorded proxy to a different cell, rejects duplicate installs of the same type, and adjusts related cell metrics.
- Genome and part records, plus notebook entries, are included in the archive/import workflow. Import checks for required genome and part fields and merges records rather than replacing the current archive.

It is important to keep the word **proxy** explicit: these records transfer a measured model value, not a physical organelle or an independently functioning biological component.

## Minimal recommendations

1. **Clarify the two simulation tracks before expanding them.** Label aggregate-world generations separately from plate-cell generations in the UI and notes. If they are meant to represent the same population, make that connection explicit; otherwise, present them as separate scales or experiments. This is the most consequential clarity improvement and does not require a rewrite.

2. **Make the simulation’s biological assumptions visible in the data.** Add a small model/version or interpretation field to exported records and part records, and show concise explanations for proxy measurements. Preserve existing record fields and add optional metadata so older local archives and imports remain usable.

3. **Improve biological grounding incrementally at the trait layer.** `traitMap()` currently maps a small set of hand-authored gene annotations and activity values directly to traits; gene sequence, regulation, and expression are simplified. A contained next step is to document that mapping and introduce a small number of explicit phenotype rules—such as how nutrient availability affects growth—rather than presenting the current direct mapping as a general biological mechanism.

4. **Give ecosystem dynamics a modest explicit structure.** The current environment and population measures provide a foundation, but much of the simulation is scalar. Add a few named organism or ecological roles and explicit resource or interaction rules before adding many new metrics. This can build on the current seeded random-number approach and existing history/events.

5. **Keep cell-part transfer intact while making compatibility clear.** Retain `archiveCellPart()` and `installCellPart()` and their provenance. Add a compatibility or organism-context label only if the model later introduces distinct cell types; avoid implying that a component is universally interchangeable across organisms.

These steps preserve the existing archive, transfer, persistence, and UI architecture while making the model’s biological scope and simulation scales easier to understand.
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Rework GENESIS into a procedurally generated game grounded in real-life biology, rather than an educational simulation.

## Requirements
- Make the game procedurally generated and biologically grounded.
- Distinguish accurate biological processes from visual-only elements.
- Preserve the cellular-part archive and transfer work.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not actual organelles or biological treatments.
- No broader redesign decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cellular-part archive and transfer features were previously implemented and browser-verified.

### Active
- Inspect and redesign game systems and framing to create a coherent procedurally generated biological world.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current game systems and identify changes needed to shift from educational-simulation framing to procedural generation grounded in real biology.
2. Implement the redesign and verify it in the browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, simulation, archive, and UI actions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and simulation framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `style.css` have uncommitted changes from earlier cellular-part work; preserve these.
- Procedural generation currently varies a deterministic educational model rather than generating a coherent biological world.
- `app.js` uses a seeded RNG, invented gene-like records and custom translation, plus lab protocols such as DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, sequencing, and CRISPR edit simulation.
- `tick()` advances the global population/genome model while `advancePlateCells()` separately advances plate cells; they do not represent one coherent evolving population.
- State initialization uses `initialState(seed, source)`; genome and plate data are built with `makeGenome(...)` and `makePlateState(...)`.
- `makeGenome` creates 8–11 genes from invented functions and random noncoding sequence; `advancePlateCells()` independently evolves plate cells using genome traits, environmental stress, and cellular-part proxies.
- Overview framing describes “A self-contained microbial world, evolving under observation”; the wet lab presents simplified procedures against the organism’s “actual genome.”
- Latest recorded browser screenshot: `screenshots/cell-observatory.jpg` (1050×793); a non-blocking `/favicon.ico` 404 was noted.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS into a procedurally generated game grounded in real-life biology, rather than an educational simulation.

## Requirements
- Make the game procedurally generated and biologically grounded.
- Distinguish accurate biological processes from visual-only elements.
- Preserve the cellular-part archive and transfer work.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not actual organelles or biological treatments.
- No broader redesign decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cellular-part archive and transfer features were previously implemented and browser-verified.

### Active
- Inspect and redesign game systems and framing to create a coherent procedurally generated biological world.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect current game systems and identify changes needed to shift from educational-simulation framing to procedural generation grounded in real biology.
2. Implement the redesign and verify it in the browser.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Game logic, simulation, archive, and UI actions.
- `index.html`: Game interface and simulation framing.
- `style.css`: Interface styling.
- `README.md`: Project overview.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `style.css` have uncommitted changes from earlier cellular-part work; preserve these.
- Procedural generation currently varies a deterministic educational model rather than generating a coherent biological world.
- `app.js` uses a seeded RNG, invented gene-like records and custom translation, plus lab protocols such as DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, sequencing, and CRISPR edit simulation.
- `tick()` advances the global population/genome model while `advancePlateCells()` separately advances plate cells; they do not represent one coherent evolving population.
- State initialization uses `initialState(seed, source)`; genome and plate data are built with `makeGenome(...)` and `makePlateState(...)`.
- `makeGenome` creates 8–11 genes from invented functions and random noncoding sequence; `advancePlateCells()` independently evolves plate cells using genome traits, environmental stress, and cellular-part proxies.
- Overview framing describes “A self-contained microbial world, evolving under observation”; the wet lab presents simplified procedures against the organism’s “actual genome.”
- Latest recorded browser screenshot: `screenshots/cell-observatory.jpg` (1050×793); a non-blocking `/favicon.ico` 404 was noted.
- Recent inspection confirmed the working tree has uncommitted changes in `app.js` and `style.css` (19 insertions, 8 deletions); no redesign changes were made.

## Objective
- Rework GENESIS into a procedurally generated game grounded in real-life biology, rather than an educational simulation.

## Requirements
- Make the game procedurally generated and biologically grounded.
- Distinguish accurate biological processes from visual-only elements.
- Preserve the cellular-part archive and transfer work.

## Decisions
- Cellular-part records are educational model proxies, not actual organelles or biological treatments.
- No broader redesign decisions have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Cellular-part archive and transfer features were previously implemented and browser-verified.
- Existing code and UI were inspected to identify simulation, genome, plate, and laboratory systems.

### Active
- Redesigning game systems and framing so procedural generation creates a coherent biological world.
- Reconciling the global population/genome simulation with independently evolving plate cells.
- Updating interface language that presents the project as an educational model or lab simulation.

<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## GENESIS

GENESIS is a procedurally generated microbial-world game. Each run builds a new environment and population, then explores how inherited variation and environmental pressures shape the organisms over time.

The biology is intentionally a **model, not a laboratory simulator**. Concepts such as DNA inheritance, mutation, gene expression, cell division, and natural selection are grounded in real biology, but are simplified into game rules and do not predict real organisms. The generated landscape, resource fields, visual cell structures, and time scale are presentation and gameplay abstractions. Cellular-part archive entries are educational model proxies—not real organelles, treatments, or transferable biological material.
